title: Kɛlɛbawɲuɲu ni masayaɲu
bridge: Espaɲe kan, kɛlɛbawɲuɲu ma fɔlɔ fana ka sira dɔn 'Hola' n'a 'Buenos días'. Masayaɲu ma fɔlɔ fana ka sira dɔn 'Me llamo...' n'a 'Soy...'. Aɲɲeman kan, kɛlɛbawɲuɲu ma fɔlɔ fana ka sira dɔn 'Hello' n'a 'Good morning'. Masayaɲu ma fɔlɔ fana ka sira dɔn 'My name is...' n'a 'I am...'. Kɛlɛya la ka sɔrɔ la, aɲɲeman kan, i tun tɛna sira dɔn 'I am called...' (walisa i jigi ka tɛmɛ jɔsɔra, o tɛ jigi ka tɛmɛ yɔrɔ a kan kɛlɛbawɲuɲu fɔlɔw la). Fɛɛrɛ fɛɛrɛ, taaɲɛgɛlɔn fɛ, aɲɲeman kan, i tun tɛna sira dɔn 'How are you called?' kɛlɛya la ka sɔrɔ 'What is your name?'.
rule: Kɛlɛbawɲuɲu ma sira dɔn: 'Hello' (Hola), 'Hi' (jɔn ka tɛmɛ yɔrɔ), 'Good morning' (Buenos días), 'Good afternoon' (Buenas tardes), 'Good evening' (Buenas noches). Masayaɲu ma sira dɔn: 'My name is...' (Me llamo...) n'a 'I am...' (Soy...). Kɛlɛya la ka sɔrɔ: 'What is your name?' (¿Cómo te llamas?). Kɛlɛbawɲuɲu fɔlɔw la ka sɔrɔ: 'Nice to meet you' (Encantado/a de conocerte) ni kɛlɛya la ka sɔrɔ 'Nice to meet you too'. Kɛlɛya ma sira dɔn: 'Goodbye', 'Bye', 'See you later'.

common_error.explanation: Espaɲe kan, i sira dɔn 'Me llamo Anna', nka, aɲɲeman kan, masayaɲu fɔlɔw la ka sɔrɔ 'My name is...' n'a 'I am...'. 'I am called' jigi ka tɛmɛ jɔsɔra, o tɛ jigi ka tɛmɛ yɔrɔ kɛlɛbawɲuɲu fɔlɔw la.

examples.note: Kɛlɛbawɲuɲu fɔlɔ
Masayaɲu fɔlɔ
Kɛlɛya la ka sɔrɔ fɔlɔ
Kɛlɛya ma jɔn

title: Kɛlɛba kɛlɛsiw bɛɛminw (jili, alaka, sigi)
bridge: Espaɲɛ kan, jili bɛɛminw ye ko 'Tengo 25 años' (k'a 'tener' tɔgɔ la), nka, angɛlɛ kan ye ko 'I am 25 years old' (k'a 'to be' tɔgɔ la). Alaka bɛɛminw ye ko 'Soy español' (muso bɛɛ minw ye ko 'Soy española', kaŋ a ta fɔlɔ muso tɛ), nka, angɛlɛ kan ye ko 'I am Spanish'. Sigi bɛɛminw ye ko 'Soy profesor' (muso bɛɛ minw ye ko 'Soy profesora', kaŋ a ta fɔlɔ muso tɛ), nka, angɛlɛ kan ye ko 'I am a teacher'.
rule: Jili bɛɛminw: 'I am [jili] years old' (tɛmɛtɛw: I am 25 years old). Alaka bɛɛminw: 'I am [alaka]' (tɛmɛtɛw: I am Spanish, I am Mexican). Sigi bɛɛminw: 'I am a/an [sigi]' (tɛmɛtɛw: I am a doctor, I am an engineer). Fɔlɔw bɛɛminw: 'How old are you?' (Jili laani?), 'Where are you from?' (Ayɛra cɛ?), 'What do you do?' (I ka nɔgɔya i jɛ?) tɩ 'What is your job?'.

common_error.explanation: Espaɲɛ kan, jili bɛɛminw ye ko 'Tengo 25 años' k'a 'tener' tɔgɔ la, nka, angɛlɛ kan ye ko 'to be' tɔgɔ la jili bɛɛminw. A b'a yɛmɔ gɛlɛsiw bɛɛminw espaɲɛ kanbeew fɔ.

examples.note: I k'a 'to be' tɔgɔ la jili bɛɛminw.
Muso tɛ alaka bɛɛminw ye.
'A' tɩ 'an' fɔlɔw ka sigi bɛɛminw ye.
Fɔlɔw ye ayɛra cɛ.

title: Describe objects and people (basic)
bridge: A taali ɲɛfɛ, kɛlɛya tile bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ ciden sɔrɔ kɛlɛya kan: 'un coche rojo', 'una chica alta'. A anglesikan, ciden bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ kɛlɛya jɛn: 'a red car', 'a tall girl'. O bɛ se ka tɛmɛ a bɛ ka tɔgɔ 'to be' ka tɛmɛw kanw (She is tall) kɛ 'have got' ka tɛmɛw kanw (She has got blue eyes).
rule: Kɛlɛya tile bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ: 1) Ciden + kɛlɛya (a big house). 2) Kɔfɛ + tɛmɛ 'to be' + ciden (The house is big). 3) Kɔfɛ + 'have/has got' + tɛmɛw kan (She has got long hair). Cidenw tile bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ: big (dɔn), small (kɛlɛ), tall (saba), short (kɛlɛ), beautiful (jɛn), old (kɛlɛ), young (jɔn), fast (kulun), slow (kɛlɛ).

concept_examples.translation: A bɛ ka tɛmɛw kan farafiiri.

common_error.explanation: A taali ɲɛfɛ, ciden bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ kɛlɛya kan (un coche rojo), nka a anglesikan, ciden bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ kɛlɛya jɛn (a red car). O bɛ se ka tɛmɛw kanw bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ hispanohablantes fɛ.

examples.note: Ciden bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ kɛlɛya jɛn.
O bɛ se ka tɛmɛ a bɛ ka tɔgɔ 'to be' ka tɛmɛw kanw.
O bɛ se ka tɛmɛ a bɛ ka tɔgɔ 'have got' ka tɛmɛw kanw fɛn.

examples.original: My brother is young and he has got green eyes.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ ˈbrʌðə ɪz jʌŋ ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ɡriːn aɪz/
examples.translation: Mi hermano es joven y tiene ojos verdes.
examples.note: 'to be' na 'have got' bɛɛn bɛ yɔrɔ.

title: Talk about daily routines
bridge: Bamanakan, kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu bɛ se ka jamana kan: 'Mɛ be sɔgɔsɔgɔni 7, mɛ ka kulisa bɛn na mɛ ka jɔya taama'. Angalɛkan, kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu bɛ se ka jamana kan: 'I get up at 7, have breakfast and go to work'. Kɔrɔsiw bɛ yɛrɛ fana ka taa, angalɛkan bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu bɛ sɛbɛn 'at' jamana tɔgɔ (at 7 o'clock), 'in' bɛɛ ka tɔgɔ la (in the morning) na 'on' bɛɛ ka tɔgɔ la (on Monday). Kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu bɛ sɛbɛn kɛlɛvɛlɛsiw bɛɛ ka tɔgɔ la 'always', 'usually', 'sometimes' masaya kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔw fɛ.
rule: Kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw: 1) Bɛ se ka jamana kan (I get up, she works). 2) Bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu: 'at' + jamana (at 8 am), 'in' + bɛɛ ka tɔgɔ la (in the morning), 'on' + bɛɛ ka tɔgɔ la (on Friday). 3) Bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu kɛlɛvɛlɛsiw masaya kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔw fɛ (I always eat breakfast). 4) Kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu: 'What time do you get up?' an ka 'When do you have lunch?'.

concept_examples.text: She usually has breakfast at 8 am.
concept_examples.translation: An ka sɔgɔsɔgɔni 8 sɔgɔsɔgɔni a be kulisa bɛn.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˈjuːʒuəli hæz ˈbrekfəst æt eɪt æm/

concept_examples.text: We go to work at 9 in the morning.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛ ka jɔya taama 9 sɔgɔsɔgɔni a be sɔgɔsɔgɔni.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ɡəʊ tə wɜːk æt naɪn ɪn ðə ˈmɔːnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: What time do you have dinner?
concept_examples.translation: Jamana nini be ka kulisa bɛn?

common_error.wrong: I am eating breakfast every morning.
common_error.explanation: Bamanakan, kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu, an bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔw fɛ ('mɛ ka kulisa bɛn sɔgɔsɔgɔni kɔlɔsi'), angalɛkan, kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu, an bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔw fɛ, o bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu kɛlɛvɛlɛsiw bɛɛ ka tɔgɔ la.

examples.note: Kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔ kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔ fɛ.

examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv lʌntʃ æt wʌn piː em/
examples.note: An bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu 'at' jamana tɔgɔ fɛ.

examples.translation: An ka kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔ o bɛ se ka jɔn ka kɛlɛ.
examples.note: Kɛlɛvɛlɛsi masaya kɛlɛsi kɛnɛmɔgɔ fɛ.

levels.label: Questions about routines
levels.translation: Kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu

examples.original: What time do you go to bed?
examples.phonetic: /wɒt taɪm duː juː ɡəʊ tə bed/
examples.translation: Jamana nini be ka jɔya taama?
examples.note: Kɔfale bɛ se ka jamana kanw dɔgɔbaw kanu 'what time' + do/does fɛ.

title: Ka ci dɔgɔ kanu (N ka ci dɔgɔ / N’ ka ci dɔgɔ kelen)
bridge: Espagnol la, ka ci dɔgɔ kanu ye ko mun ye verb 'gustar' ye: 'Me gusta la pizza' (literalement 'La pizza me gusta a mí'). Anglais la, mun ye verb 'like' ye ko sujet + like + objet structure: 'I like pizza'. La difference fana ye ko espagnol la, verb 'gustar' ye objet ye dɔgɔ kanu (me gusta la pizza, me gustan las pizzas), anglais la 'like' ye sujet ye dɔgɔ kanu (I like pizza, He likes pizza). Ye fana mɔgɔkɔrɔfilɛ mun lo ko ka ci dɔgɔ kanu ye ko 'I don't like' (no me gusta).
rule: Ka ci dɔgɔ kanu: 1) Afirmativo: I/you/we/they like + objet (I like coffee). He/she/it likes + objet (She likes coffee). 2) Negativo: I/you/we/they don't like (I don't like tea). He/she/it doesn't like (He doesn't like tea). 3) Questions: Do you like...? (¿Te gusta...?), Does she like...? (¿Le gusta a ella...?). 4) Ka fɔlɔ: 'I like it very much' (Me gusta mucho) o 'I really like it' (Me gusta mucho).

concept_examples.translation: N ka ci dɔgɔ pizza ye.
A ye ka ci dɔgɔ ka taa ye.
Mun ka ci dɔgɔ tɛɛmɛn ye.

common_error.explanation: Espagnol la, adverb 'mucho' ye verb cɔɔla jati: 'Me gusta mucho la pizza'. Anglais la, adverb 'very much' ye tɛmɛ jɔɔla kɔfɛ o objet cɔɔla jati: 'I like pizza very much'. A ye verb nɔgɔnyɛɛla jati fɛɛn na.

examples.translation: N ka ci dɔgɔ chocolat ye.
examples.note: Verb 'like' ye fɔlɔwuli form.

examples.translation: A ye ka ci dɔgɔ futbolu ye.
examples.note: Mun ye -s jɔɔla jati ko u ye jamana.

examples.translation: A ye ka ci dɔgɔ kafi ye.
examples.note: Mun ye 'doesn't' + verb fɔlɔwuli.
Taa ko 'do' + sujet + verb fɔlɔwuli.

title: Ask for and give prices
bridge: A tɛ baara ne, k’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye ko ‘How much is it?’ (jɛnɲɔgɔ) n’a ‘How much are they?’ (jɛnɲɔgɔw ye). An b’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye ko ‘How much does it cost?’. Kɔrɔsi tɛ b’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘to be’ n’a ‘cost’ an ka ‘does’ jati fɔ. K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘It is [number] dollars/euros’ n’a ‘It costs [number]’.
rule: K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye: 1) ‘How much is it?’ (jɛnɲɔgɔ wɔrɔ) n’a ‘How much are they?’ (jɛnɲɔgɔw ye). 2) ‘How much does it cost?’. 3) ‘How much is the T-shirt?’. K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘It is 25 dollars’ n’a ‘It costs 25 dollars’. K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye, an b’a ‘to be’ n’a ‘does’ + ‘cost’ jati fɔ.

concept_examples.translation: A y’a ciyaara jɛnɲɔgɔw ye za kɛrɛsɛw ye?

common_error.explanation: A tɛ baara ne, an ka ‘does’ jati fɔ k’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘cost’ jati fɔ. Kɔrɔsi tɛ esikɛnya bato b’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘does’ jati fɔ.

levels.label: Ask price with 'to be'
levels.translation: K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘to be’

examples.translation: A y’a ciyaara jɛnɲɔgɔ wɔrɔ ka tiliw ye?
examples.note: An b’a ‘to be’ k’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye.

levels.label: Ask price with 'cost'
levels.translation: K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye k’a ‘cost’

examples.original: How much does the bag cost?
examples.translation: A y’a ciyaara ka saba ye?
examples.note: An b’a ‘does’ + ‘cost’ k’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye.

levels.label: Give price
levels.translation: K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye

examples.note: An b’a ‘costs’ a ka jɛnɲɔgɔ wɔrɔ fɔ.

levels.label: Plural questions
levels.translation: K’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye jɛnɲɔgɔw ye

examples.translation: A y’a ciyaara jɛnɲɔgɔw ye za tɛnɛw ye?
examples.note: An b’a ‘are’ k’a flɛ ka ciyaara b’a ye jɛnɲɔgɔw ye.

title: Indicate location of places / Ka bɔri kelenw ye
bridge: A taali gi, kelenw bɔri kanw ye fana ka taa 'A ka bɔri ye...', 'A yɛrɛ laa banki ye', 'A manja stasɔɔn ye'. A lɔnnikɛlaw ye, an ka taa ka kɛlɛ ka bɔri ye fana 'on', 'in', 'at', 'next to', 'near', 'opposite', 'behind', 'in front of'. Hispanifɛmɔgɔw maa ka taa 'en' ka taa kelenw bɔriw ye fana, nka, a lɔnnikɛlaw ye, kɛlɛ ka bɔri ye fana ka taa ka tɛmɛ a ka bɔri ye fana ka taa. O fɛɛw ka taa, kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa ka taa 'to be' (It is...).
rule: Kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa: 1) Taa 'to be' (The bank is...). 2) Kɛlɛ ka bɔri ye fana: 'on' (ka bɔri ye fana ka taa, ka bɔri ye fana ka taa), 'in' (ka bɔri ye fana ka taa), 'at' (ka bɔri ye fana ka taa), 'next to' (yɛrɛ laa), 'near' (manja), 'opposite' (ka bɔri ye fana ka taa), 'behind' (ka bɔri ye fana ka taa), 'in front of' (ka bɔri ye fana ka taa). 3) Ka bɔri ye fana ka taa: 'Where is the...?' (Kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa?) o 'Is there a... near here?' (A bɔri ye fana manja aw ye?)

concept_examples.text: The supermarket is near the park.
concept_examples.translation: Super marchɛ a manja parkɛ ye.

concept_examples.text: The school is next to the church.
concept_examples.translation: Sikola a yɛrɛ laa zikikɛlaw ye.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə skuːl ɪz nekst tə ðə tʃɜːtʃ/

concept_examples.text: The pharmacy is on Main Street.
concept_examples.translation: Farmasi a ka bɔri ye Principali sira ye.
Kelenw bɔri ye bus stasɔɔn a ye?

common_error.explanation: A taali gi, an ka taa 'A ka bɔri ye kɔnɔ' nka an ka taa ka kɛlɛ ka bɔri ye fana. A lɔnnikɛlaw ye, 'It' o 'He/She' ka taa ka taa ka bɔri ye fana. A fɛɛw ka taa, 'en la kɔnɔ' ka taa 'on the corner' (aw ka taa 'in the corner') sira kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa sira kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa.

levels.label: Basic location with 'in'
levels.translation: Kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa 'in'

examples.original: The cat is in the garden.
examples.translation: Musu a ka bɔri ye jɛnɛ ye.
examples.note: An ka taa 'in' ka taa kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa.

levels.label: Location with 'next to'
levels.translation: Kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa 'next to'

examples.original: The restaurant is next to the hotel.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈrestrɒnt ɪz nekst tə ðə həʊˈtel/
examples.translation: Restɔrɔ a yɛrɛ laa oteli ye.
examples.note: An ka taa 'next to' ka taa yɛrɛ laa kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa.

levels.label: Location with 'near' and 'opposite'
levels.translation: Kelenw bɔri ye fana ka taa 'near' la 'opposite'

examples.original: The bank is opposite the park.
examples.translation: Banki a ka bɔri ye parkɛ ye.
examples.note: An ka taa 'opposite' ka taa ka bɔri ye fana ka taa.

examples.translation: Kelenw bɔri ye komandisiri a ye?
examples.note: Fajeri ka taa 'Where' ka taa.
